A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–D. Their equations, six figures and Table 1 support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original GFlowNet training experiments on hypergrid and permutation environments, including numerical results in Table 1 and experimental curves in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original hypergrid and permutation experiments, including Table 1 and the main-text and appendix learning curves.

M1.justification: The policy formulation, DB/SDB losses, flow versus log-flow scaling and state-flow regularization in Equation 12 are unchanged. The appendix proof revisions do not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate 7×7 and 20×20×20×20 hypergrids and permutations of lengths 4, 8 and 20, including Appendix D. Environment transitions and reward distributions are unchanged.

E2.justification: The same DB and SDB loss variants participate in the corresponding comparisons in Table 1 and Figures 1, 2 and 4–6. No evaluated comparator is added, removed or replaced.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same metrics, evaluation windows, model configurations and training procedures. Budgets remain two million sampled trajectories for hypergrids and 100,000 training iterations for permutations.

E4.justification: The fixed-versus-trainable backward-policy comparisons, removal-of-regularization analysis in Figure 4 and regularization-strength sweep in Figure 5 are retained unchanged, as is the small-permutation analysis in Figure 6.

E5.justification: Table 1 reports means and standard deviations across three random seeds in both versions. The uncertainty reporting and plotted bands are unchanged; no additional statistical procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 values and all plotted curves are unchanged. For example, at permutation length 20 and regularization strength 10^-5, log-flow DB and SDB retain C(k) L1 errors of 0.017 ± 0.002 and 0.014 ± 0.001, respectively.

T1.justification: Appendices A.2 and A.4 repair derivations for Propositions 3.6 and 3.8. v2 substitutes policy probabilities after conditioning on trajectory length; v3 instead uses explicit absorbing Markov chains and finite-expectation/Fubini arguments. These are localized proof corrections; the assumptions and formal result statements remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, five introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about non-acyclic GFlowNet theory, backward policies, loss stability, state-flow regularization and the entropy-regularized RL connection.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations and qualifications concerning flow-scale underestimation bias, potentially long trajectories with fixed backward policies, and the sampling-fidelity versus trajectory-length tradeoff from regularization. The corresponding discussion receives only grammatical edits.

D1.justification: Appendices B and C retain the implementation disclosures, including input encodings, MLP architectures, optimizer settings, batch sizes and evaluation details. The source-code access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning relative to prior work are unchanged. The introduction reorders the Uehara and Zhang citations without adding or removing either work.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited grammatical and punctuation corrections, removes the duplicated 'of the' in Section 4.3, standardizes time-index notation in Appendix A.1 and rewrites prose accompanying the corrected proofs. Section and appendix organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Equation 10 spacing and the proof displays in Appendices A.2 and A.4 are adjusted, producing local layout changes. All six figures and Table 1 retain their structure, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the mathematical support for Propositions 3.6 and 3.8 by replacing unjustified length-conditioned probability substitutions with explicit Markov-chain derivations and finite-expectation arguments. These targeted proof repairs and light copyediting improve rigor and clarity, while the methods, claims and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
